lines.trans: Director, it is time to go. Let's hurry.
Today's cast members are—good, they are all here.
President Kawada, could I have the expense advance, please?
Hold on just a moment. Here you go.
If the actress starts crying on set, show her this extra envelope.
In return, make sure you finish shooting everything before the day ends.
Yes, sir, understood! Copy that!
Everyone hop in the van. Make sure nobody leaves anything behind.
Hey, the delivery address on this box is wrong. Please get it right.
Mr. Muranishi, let's have another great shoot today.
All right everyone, off we go! It is the start of a monumental year.
Give it your best.

words.gram: て-form of 頑張る (work hard), used sarcastically here.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for time on the clock or a dedicated stretch of time.

examples.text: まだ少し時間があります。
examples.trans: There is still a little time.

examples.text: 楽しい時間をありがとう。
examples.trans: Thank you for the fun time.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

examples.text: 監督、時間です。急ぎましょう。
examples.trans: Director, it is time to go. Let's hurry.

examples.text: いらねえよ！嫌いなんだようなぎはよ。
examples.trans: I don't want it! I hate eel anyway.

meanings.note: Special reading きょう.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Satisfied exclamation when gearing up or finishing a task cleanly.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: 社長、仮払いお願いします。
examples.trans: President Kawada, could I have the expense advance, please?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: て-form 待って + ください is 'please wait'; causative お待たせして means 'having kept you waiting'.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

examples.text: もし女優が泣きだしたら、これを見せてください。
examples.trans: If the actress starts crying on set, show her this extra envelope.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').

examples.text: その代わり、今日中に必ず撮りきってください。
examples.trans: In return, make sure you finish shooting everything before the day ends.

examples.text: 全部買ってやる。その代わりあんたの知恵をよこせ。
examples.trans: I will buy all of them. In exchange, give me your strategic brains.

examples.text: その代わり、今日中に必ず撮りきってください。
examples.trans: In return, make sure you finish shooting everything before the day ends.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

examples.text: ただ販売するには、必ずヒットするってことを示さないと。
examples.trans: Still, to get stores to carry it, we must prove it will definitely be a hit.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 五日で十五本撮りって新記録っすよね。
examples.trans: Shooting fifteen videos in five days has got to be a new record.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

examples.text: はい、分かりました。了解です！
現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: みんな乗り込むよ。忘れ物ないようにね。
examples.trans: Everyone hop in the van. Make sure nobody leaves anything behind.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

examples.text: これ、配送先違いますよ。お願いしますよ。
examples.trans: Hey, the delivery address on this box is wrong. Please get it right.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Alone as 違う！ or 違います, means 'No, that's wrong!'.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Core adverb in set greetings like よろしくお願いします and どうぞよろしく.
Prompts someone into action or shoos them along.
Formal/polite transition; contracts to それじゃ or じゃあ in casual speech.

examples.text: それでは始めましょう。

meanings.note: Polite way to address a group of people.

examples.text: 皆さんにお知らせがあります。
examples.trans: I have an announcement for everyone.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 行く and 来る.

examples.text: それでは参りましょう。

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

examples.text: さあそれでは皆さん参りましょう！記念すべき年の始まりです。
examples.trans: All right everyone, off we go! It is the start of a monumental year.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: 頑張ります! is the classic cheerful commitment when starting a job or task.

examples.trans: I will do my best today too.
Do your best on the exam!

meanings.note: Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.
